adidas-adizero-adios-8: Light, low-stack and fast with good ground feel; little stability, and a few find it dead.
adidas-adizero-adios-9: Sock-like upper and durable outsole for track and short races; hard on the legs with heavy use.
adidas-adizero-adios-pro-4: Soft, bouncy and fast with a comfier upper than before; the toe box runs narrow, so many size up.
adidas-adizero-adios-pro-5: Smoother and steadier than its predecessor, more super trainer; some find the fit narrow.
adidas-adizero-boston-12: Firm, very durable and grippy for tempo days; the main complaint is heel slip and poor lockdown.
adidas-adizero-boston-13: Stable, firm tempo shoe with secure lockdown; some find it stiff, and the toe box is tapered.
adidas-adizero-evo-sl: Light, bouncy and fun at speed; wobbly at slow paces, with ankle soreness on longer runs.
adidas-adizero-sl2: Soft, bouncy and responsive; the tight midfoot gives blisters, so several size up.
adidas-hyperboost-edge: Bouncy, cushioned ride for easy and long runs; the upper draws most complaints as hot or tight.
adidas-supernova-rise-2: Durable everyday trainer that doubles for walking, often found on sale; firm or flat for speed.
altra-olympus-275: Well cushioned, grippy and tough for long technical days; a wide shape and a heel that folds down.
asics-gel-trabuco-12: Reliable, grippy mixed-trail shoe; the ride is dull and the upper can give out first.
asics-glideride-max: Cushioned daily trainer for easy and long runs that can still pick up the pace; a bit plain to some.
asics-megablast: Bouncy, very durable all-rounder; the narrow, low toe box blisters pinky toes.
brooks-cascadia-19: Plush, grippy trail shoe liked by wide-footed and ultra runners; a few fans dislike the softer feel.
brooks-ghost-amp: Comfortable, soft and springy from easy runs to tempo.
dynafish-xiaonian: Light, stable and bouncy, with several reporting around 1,000 km; stock laces and thin insole annoy.
hoka-mach-6: Light, responsive daily and tempo shoe; the narrow fit sends many to the wide version.
hoka-mach-x-2: Light and springy for tempo and long runs; a good share get heel slip and Achilles blisters.
hoka-rocket-x-3: Stable, not-too-aggressive racer for marathons and workouts; a few find the foam unexciting.
hoka-speedgoat-7: Roomy and comfortable for long, hilly runs; the upper fails early, with holes and split stitching.
hoka-tecton-x-3: Plated, protective ultra shoe with a roomy toe box; unstable for some, and weak on technical ground.
li-ning-red-hare-9-ultra: Bouncy, well-cushioned and fun for long runs; tight for some and short on stability.
mizuno-neo-zen: Soft, fun daily trainer with lively foam; unstable for some, and mushy at faster paces.
new-balance-fuelcell-rebel-v5: Roomy, lively daily shoe, but others found it too soft for speed or felt the foam go flat early.
nike-alphafly-3: Comfortable, stable racer with a roomy toe box and good heel hold; many notice the noise.
nike-pegasus-plus: Light, lively and secure for tempo and fast daily runs; snug and tapered for some.
nike-ultrafly: Stable, roomy shoe for smooth trails; the stiff plate bothers some, and technical ground is weak.
nike-vomero-plus: Very plush, durable and bouncy for easy and long runs; unstable on uneven ground or turns.
nike-vomero-premium: Very plush, joint-friendly cushioning for easy long runs; heavy, and the stack feels wobbly to some.
nike-zegama-2: Cushioned, grippy trail shoe that lasts; stability splits, with some rolling ankles, and it's bulky.
nike-zoom-fly-6: Responsive tempo shoe with a no-fuss upper that many run for hundreds of kilometres; firm for some.
on-cloudmonster-3-hyper: Firmer-side, protective trainer that keeps the legs fresh.
on-cloudmonster-hyper: Roomy upper and springy ride that shines at speed; a few got blisters or heel pain.
puma-deviate-nitro-elite-3: Fast, bouncy racer with PBs from 5K to marathon; narrow, so it suits narrower feet best.
puma-deviate-nitro-elite-4: Stable, fast racer that also handles long runs and workouts; a few preferred the previous version.
puma-fast-r-nitro-elite-3: Very light and fast, with PBs from 5K up; snug fit, and several find it punishing on the calves.
puma-magmax-nitro: Bouncy, protective and durable with a wide stable base; the weight feels clunky when speeding up.
puma-magmax-nitro-2: Roomy fit much better than the original, good for recovery runs; the foam is firm and dense.
puma-velocity-nitro-4: Responsive, durable daily trainer that can pick up the pace; the midfoot fit is narrow and snug.
salomon-aero-glide-3: Light, bouncy daily trainer from easy to tempo; fit varies, with some finding the midfoot narrow.
salomon-aero-glide-3-grvl: Comfortable, grippy and cushioned on gravel and as a road trainer; a few found it firm at first.
salomon-genesis: Durable all-round trail shoe trusted for ultras; narrow forefoot for some, and a few get heel slip.
salomon-s-lab-genesis: Precise, secure fit and grip on technical terrain, rated well above the regular version.
saucony-endorphin-azura: Firm, stable, light do-it-all trainer; some find it harsh, though several say it softens.
saucony-endorphin-elite-2: Very soft, bouncy racer with a super comfortable upper; wobbly at slow speeds or in corners.
saucony-endorphin-speed-5: Firm, stable and light for speed sessions; lukewarm reactions, with several calling it flat or dull.
saucony-hurricane-25: Stable, well-cushioned shoe for easy, recovery and long runs; a few find the toe box too narrow.
saucony-ride-18: Comfortable trainer, though several find the ride flat or dead.
saucony-triumph-24: Light, soft yet bouncy trainer, livelier than earlier versions; one found it too soft at the ankle.
adidas-adizero-takumi-sen-10: Light, fast shoe for intervals and short races; the narrow, snug fit is the main gripe.
hoka-clifton-10: Soft, comfortable easy-run shoe, though a few found it firmer and wobblier than the last.
asics-superblast-2: Firm, stable and very durable, though some never warm to the stiff, heavy feel at slow paces.
nike-air-zoom-pegasus-39: Durable everyday trainer whose outsole often passes 400 miles, but the ride leans firm.
new-balance-fresh-foam-x-1080-v13: Very plush for recovery and slow long runs, but some find it mushy at faster paces.
brooks-glycerin-max: Plush yet lively, though arch and heel blisters are the most frequent complaint.
nike-pegasus-premium: Bouncy with a premium feel on easy runs; the main complaint is the weight at faster paces.
altra-timp-5: Protective, grippy and roomy at the midfoot, but several report upper blowouts or tread wear.
asics-sonicblast: Lively and peppy for tempo and interval work; a few found it too stiff and dead.
new-balance-fuelcell-supercomp-trainer-v: Responsive, stable and protective; scattered complaints include foam going dead at high mileage.
puma-magnify-nitro-2: Cushioned, durable daily shoe with a grippy outsole, but not one for fast running.
new-balance-fuelcell-propel-v4: Good-value daily trainer with some plate pop, though several had heel slip or dead foam.
brooks-glycerin-22: Comfortable, responsive road shoe for long runs, though one found the toe box narrower.
adidas-adizero-sl: Firm but durable with a grippy outsole, though some find it too harsh for easy days or long runs.
adidas-adizero-adios-pro-3: Fast, bouncy and long-lasting; the main gripe is blisters, lace bite and heel rubbing.
brooks-hyperion-tempo: Light, fast and firm with good ground feel, but unforgiving for some on slow, very long runs.
nike-vaporfly-3: Fast, light race-day shoe with a roomier forefoot; complaints are scattered, like blisters.
saucony-endorphin-speed-4: Snappy with a rocker that comes alive at pace, but the narrow fit causes toe pressure for several.
puma-deviate-pure-nitro: Versatile daily trainer with a roomy upper, though the foam is firm and some want more bounce.
asics-magic-speed-4: Light, bouncy and versatile up to the half marathon; a few find it heavy for speed work.
new-balance-fuelcell-supercomp-elite-v4: Bouncy, stable and roomy in the toe box; the main downsides are weight and some heel slip.
saucony-kinvara-pro: Stable and peppy for long runs and marathon training; a few find it heavy on longer runs.
on-cloudeclipse: Comfortable, stable and long-lasting, though squeaking is the most repeated complaint.
asics-trabuco-14: Comfortable on gravel and light trail, though it rides firmer and stiffer than some expected.
brooks-cascadia-elite: Stable, protective trail shoe with soft foam, but some find the forefoot too wide.
new-balance-fresh-foam-x-880-v14: Roomy, dependable daily trainer with a simple ride, though some find the foam lacks return.
puma-foreverrun-nitro: Cushioned, mildly stable easy-day shoe; the main downside is durability, with foam dying for some.
salomon-ultra-glide-2: Comfortable with a secure heel hold, but the midsole went flat or delaminated for several.
altra-lone-peak-9: Roomy toe box and a breathable trail feel; the main complaint is cushioning that breaks down.
new-balance-fresh-foam-x-balos: Very soft, bouncy and rockered with a sock-like upper; a few find it too soft for harder workouts.
nike-pegasus-41: Reliable, very durable daily shoe; fit splits opinion, as some find the forefoot too narrow.
on-cloudboom-strike: Fast, breathable race shoe with strong energy return, but several got blisters or heel lift.
saucony-endorphin-pro-4: Roomy, stable plated shoe for 5K to marathon, but many rate its energy return below the last.
on-cloudsurfer-7: Light, comfortable easy-run shoe with a wide toe box; squeaking is the most repeated complaint.
nike-wildhorse-8: Durable, roomy trail shoe with good traction for ultras, though it is a bit heavy.
hoka-skyward-x: Plush, bouncy and very durable, though the plate cracked for a couple of runners.
adidas-adizero-takumi-sen-11: Snappy with a soft upper and good energy return, though the narrow fit is the main downside.
nike-acg-zegama-trail: Stable with good lockdown on rocky terrain, though a few found the tall, soft stack insecure.
adidas-adizero-prime-x-2-strung: Bouncy and fast for racing; the main downside is durability, as the plate broke for a couple.
